theme.title: Return to Me
theme.summary: From the ashes to Holy Week: one step of conversion each day, fasting, prayer and almsgiving, until the Church stands with Christ at the gate of the Triduum.

topics.name: Lent
topics.summary: The season as a whole: what Lent is, fasting and almsgiving, prayer, confession, the desert, the works of mercy, Holy Week and the saints of Lent.

levels.title: The Desert and the Forty Days

topics.name: Lent Challenge
topics.summary: One day of Lent at a time, from Ash Wednesday to Holy Wednesday.

levels.title: Return to Me
levels.reflection: Lent opens with ashes and with a call older than the Church. The prophet Joel tells Israel to come back to the Lord with all their heart, in fasting, weeping and mourning, and then names what matters most: rend your hearts, not your garments. The Catechism says the same of Jesus' own call to conversion: it does not aim first at outward works, but at the conversion of the heart. Fasting, prayer and almsgiving are how that change shows itself. The ashes today are not a mark of gloom. They are the sign of a people who know the one to whom they are returning is gracious and merciful.

scripture.text: Now therefore saith the Lord: Be converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning. And rend your hearts, and not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, patient and rich in mercy, and ready to repent of the evil.

saint.name: St. Ambrose
saint.reference: Epistle 41, 12, as quoted in CCC 1429
saint.text: there are water and tears: the water of Baptism and the tears of repentance.

levels.title: Choose Life
levels.reflection: Near the end of his life Moses puts the whole Law into one choice. He has set before Israel life and death, blessing and cursing, and he begs them to choose life. Christ's words in the Gospel are the same call in a harder voice: whoever will come after him must deny himself and take up his cross daily. That sounds like the road to death, and the Lord says it is the road to life, for whoever loses his life for his sake will save it. The Catechism calls taking up the cross each day the surest way of penance. Lent is not a mood. It is a daily choice.

scripture.text: I call heaven and earth to witness this day, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing. Choose therefore life, that both thou and thy seed may live:

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Confessions 10, 20, as quoted in CCC 1718
saint.text: How is it, then, that I seek you, Lord? Since in seeking you, my God, I seek a happy life, let me seek you so that my soul may live, for my body draws life from my soul and my soul draws life from you.

levels.title: The Fast I Have Chosen
levels.reflection: It is the first Friday of Lent, and Isaiah asks the hard question: what kind of fast does the Lord want? The people had fasted and wondered why God took no notice. The answer is that a fast which leaves the heart untouched, and the hungry unfed, is not the fast he has chosen. He wants chains loosed, bread dealt to the hungry, the naked covered. The Church keeps each Friday of the year in penance, in memory of the death of the Lord. Fasting is meant to open the hand as well as empty the stomach. Whatever you give up today, let it reach someone who is in need.

scripture.text: Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen? loose the bands of wickedness, undo the bundles that oppress, let them that are broken go free, and break asunder every burden. Deal thy bread to the hungry, and bring the needy and the harbourless into thy house: when thou shalt see one naked, cover him, and despise not thy own flesh.

saint.name: St. John Chrysostom
saint.reference: Homilies on 1 Corinthians 27, 4, as quoted in CCC 1397
saint.text: You have tasted the Blood of the Lord, yet you do not recognize your brother,.... You dishonor this table when you do not judge worthy of sharing your food someone judged worthy to take part in this meal.... God freed you from all your sins and invited you here, but you have not become more merciful.

levels.title: Not the Just, but Sinners
levels.reflection: Levi sat at his tax booth, a man the respectable avoided, and Jesus said two words to him: Follow me. Levi rose, left everything and made a great feast for the one who had called him. The Pharisees murmured that Jesus ate with sinners, and he answered that the sick need the physician, not the healthy. He came to call sinners to penance. The Catechism says the Church herself is at once holy and always in need of purification, so no one comes to Lent as a righteous bystander. Every one of us is at the table by mercy, and the Physician is already there.

scripture.text: And Jesus answering, said to them: They that are whole, need not the physician: but they that are sick. I came not to call the just, but sinners to penance.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Commentary on the Gospel of John 12, 13, as quoted in CCC 1458
saint.text: God indicts your sins; if you also indict them, you are joined with God.

levels.title: Led into the Desert
levels.reflection: On the first Sunday of Lent the Church goes where the Spirit led Jesus: into the desert. After his baptism he fasted forty days and forty nights, and then the tempter came with three offers, bread for his hunger, a spectacle in the Temple, the kingdoms of the world. Each time the Lord answered from Scripture and not from power. The Catechism says Jesus is the new Adam who stayed faithful where the first Adam fell, and that by the forty days of Lent the Church unites herself each year to this mystery. Whatever you are tempted by today, he has already faced it, and he won.

scripture.text: Who answered and said: It is written, Not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word that proceedeth from the mouth of God.

saint.name: St. Ambrose
saint.reference: On the Sacraments 5, 4, 30, as quoted in CCC 2852
saint.text: The Lord who has taken away your sin and pardoned your faults also protects you and keeps you from the wiles of your adversary the devil, so that the enemy, who is accustomed to leading into sin, may not surprise you. One who entrusts himself to God does not dread the devil.

levels.title: I Was Hungry
levels.reflection: The Church puts the last judgment before us at the very start of Lent, and its test is surprisingly plain. The king does not ask about visions or great works. He asks whether we fed the hungry, gave drink to the thirsty, took in the stranger, clothed the naked, and visited the sick and the prisoner. Whatever was done to the least of his brethren, he says, was done to him. The Catechism calls almsgiving one of the chief witnesses to fraternal charity. Lent's fasting is not meant to make us thin. It is meant to make us look up and see who is hungry.

scripture.text: And the king answering, shall say to them: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Sermon 18, 4, as quoted in CCC 1039
saint.text: I placed my poor little ones on earth for you. I as their head was seated in heaven at the right hand of my Father - but on earth my members were suffering, my members on earth were in need.

levels.title: Teach Us to Pray
levels.reflection: Jesus gives the Our Father in the same chapter of Matthew that sets out fasting and almsgiving, so the three pillars of Lent stand together there. He warns that prayer is not a matter of many words, for the Father knows what we need before we ask. Then he gives us seven petitions to say. The Catechism calls the Lord's Prayer the summary of the whole gospel, and notes how early the Church closed it with praise. Notice the heart of it: forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. Lent's prayer begins with the words he gave, and with the promise that our Father is listening.

scripture.text: And when you are praying, speak not much, as the heathens. For they think that in their much speaking they may be heard. Be not you therefore like to them, for your Father knoweth what is needful for you, before you ask him. Thus therefore shall you pray: Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name.

saint.name: St. John Chrysostom
saint.reference: Homilies on Matthew 19, 4, as quoted in CCC 2768
saint.text: [The Lord] teaches us to make prayer in common for all our brethren. For he did not say "my Father" who art in heaven, but "our" Father, offering petitions for the common body.

levels.title: Nineveh Repents
levels.reflection: Jonah may be the most reluctant preacher in Scripture, and yet his short sermon turns a whole city. The men of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least. God saw their works, saw that they had turned from their evil way, and had mercy. Jesus points to Nineveh as a reproach to his own generation, for they did penance at the preaching of Jonah, and now one greater than Jonah is here. Penance is never wasted. Through the keys Christ gave her, the Church forgives sins, so no one is too far gone to turn back.

scripture.text: And the men of Ninive believed in God: and they proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Sermon 214, 11, as quoted in CCC 981
saint.text: In this Church, the soul dead through sin comes back to life in order to live with Christ, whose grace has saved us.

levels.title: Ask, Seek, Knock
levels.reflection: Lent can feel like a list of things to give up, but today's Gospel turns it into a conversation. Ask, and it shall be given; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened. Jesus rests the promise on something we already know: if even sinful parents give good gifts to their children, how much more will the Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him. The Catechism teaches that prayer is the raising of the mind and heart to God, and that humility is its foundation. Come to the Father as a child comes, with empty hands and a plain request.

scripture.text: Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you. For every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shall be opened.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Letter 130, 8, 17, as quoted in CCC 2737
saint.text: God wills that our desire should be exercised in prayer, that we may be able to receive what he is prepared to give.

levels.title: No Pleasure in Death
levels.reflection: Through Ezekiel the Lord asks a question that settles who he is: is it his will that a sinner should die, and not that he should be converted from his ways and live? The prophet is plain that a wicked man who turns from his wickedness and does justice shall save his soul alive. Jesus carries the same mercy into the New Law. If you remember at the altar that your brother has something against you, he says, leave your gift there and go first to be reconciled. The Church also calls the sacrament of Penance the sacrament of Reconciliation, and Lent is a good time to go.

scripture.text: Is it my will that a sinner should die, saith the Lord God, and not that he should be converted from his ways, and live?

saint.name: St. Cyprian
saint.reference: On the Lord's Prayer 23, as quoted in CCC 2845
saint.text: God does not accept the sacrifice of a sower of disunion, but commands that he depart from the altar so that he may first be reconciled with his brother. For God can be appeased only by prayers that make peace.

levels.title: Love Your Enemies
levels.reflection: The Gospel for the last day of this first full week of Lent asks the hardest thing yet: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who persecute you. Jesus gives the reason. The Father makes his sun rise on the good and the bad, and sends rain on the just and the unjust, and his children should look like him. The Catechism points to the cross, where Christ died for us while we were still enemies, and says he asks us to love as he does. Perfection here does not mean being faultless. It means loving as the Father loves.

scripture.text: But I say to you, Love your enemies: do good to them that hate you: and pray for them that persecute and calumniate you: That you may be the children of your Father who is in heaven, who maketh his sun to rise upon the good, and bad, and raineth upon the just and the unjust.

saint.name: St. Cyprian
saint.reference: On the Lord's Prayer 11, as quoted in CCC 2784
saint.text: You cannot call the God of all kindness your Father if you preserve a cruel and inhuman heart; for in this case you no longer have in you the marks of the heavenly Father's kindness.

levels.title: Listen to Him
levels.reflection: Midway through the road to Jerusalem the Church climbs a mountain. Jesus takes Peter, James and John apart and is transfigured before them, his garments shining white. A cloud overshadows them, and the Father's voice says what he said at the Jordan: this is my beloved Son, hear him. The Catechism notes that Jesus speaks there with Moses and Elijah of his departure, so that the disciples might know the cross is part of the plan, and not a defeat. Peter wanted to stay. The Lord leads them down again, because the glory is the end of the road and not the road.

scripture.text: And there was a cloud overshadowing them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying: This is my most beloved son; hear ye him.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Sermon 78, 6, as quoted in CCC 556
saint.text: Go down to toil on earth, to serve on earth, to be scorned and crucified on earth. Life goes down to be killed; Bread goes down to suffer hunger; the Way goes down to be exhausted on his journey; the Spring goes down to suffer thirst; and you refuse to suffer?

levels.title: Be Merciful
levels.reflection: The second week of Lent begins with a sentence from Luke that the whole Gospel hangs on: be merciful, as your Father also is merciful. Jesus does not leave it general. Judge not, and you shall not be judged; condemn not, and you shall not be condemned; forgive, and you shall be forgiven. Mercy here is not a mood but a measure, and what we give is what we will receive. The Catechism lists forgiving and bearing wrongs patiently among the spiritual works of mercy, and says even our own confessions spur us on to be merciful as he is merciful. God's mercy always goes first, and ours follows after it.

scripture.text: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: On Nature and Grace 31, as quoted in CCC 2001
saint.text: for his mercy has gone before us. It has gone before us so that we may be healed, and follows us so that once healed, we may be given life.

levels.title: White as Snow
levels.reflection: The Lord calls Israel to a courtroom and then offers something no courtroom does: come, and though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be made as white as snow. The first condition is to wash and be clean, and to cease to do perversely. In the Gospel Jesus turns to the opposite danger, the religion of being seen, and says that the greatest among you shall be your servant, for whoever humbles himself shall be exalted. The Catechism links humility with poverty in spirit. Lent asks us to bring our scarlet to the Lord, trusting that he turns it into snow.

scripture.text: And then come, and accuse me, saith the Lord: if your sins be as scarlet, they shall be made as white as snow: and if they be red as crimson, they shall be white as wool.

saint.name: St. Gregory of Nyssa
saint.reference: On the Beatitudes 1, as quoted in CCC 2546
saint.text: The Word speaks of voluntary humility as "poverty in spirit"; the Apostle gives an example of God's poverty when he says: "For your sakes he became poor."

levels.title: Not to Be Served
levels.reflection: James and John ask for the best seats in the kingdom, and Jesus answers with a question: can you drink the chalice that I shall drink? They say they can, not knowing what they say. He then turns the ambition of the Twelve upside down. Among the Gentiles the great exercise authority, but it shall not be so among you. Whoever would be greater must be your minister. The Son of man himself came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a redemption for many. The Catechism says that this sums up Christ's whole mission. In Lent, greatness is measured by service.

scripture.text: Even as the Son of man is not come to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a redemption for many.

saint.name: St. Fulgentius of Ruspe
saint.reference: Against Fabian 28, 16-19, as quoted in CCC 1394
saint.text: Having received the gift of love, let us die to sin and live for God.

levels.title: Moses and the Prophets
levels.reflection: A rich man who feasted every day and a beggar who lay at his gate: Jesus tells the story to make us see what we have grown used to not seeing. When both die, the beggar is carried by angels to Abraham's bosom, and the rich man is buried in hell. He begs that someone be sent to warn his brothers, and Abraham answers that they have Moses and the prophets. Jeremiah says the same from the other side: cursed is the man who trusts in man, and blessed the man who trusts in the Lord. The Catechism recalls that when we give to the poor we are giving what is theirs, not ours.

scripture.text: And Abraham said to him: They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

saint.name: St. John of the Cross
saint.reference: Sayings of Light and Love 64, as quoted in CCC 1022
saint.text: At the evening of life, we shall be judged on our love.

levels.title: The Rejected Stone
levels.reflection: Jesus tells the Pharisees of a man who planted a vineyard and leased it to husbandmen. He sent servants for the fruit and they were beaten, and last of all he sent his son, saying they will reverence my son. They seized him and cast him out. It is a story of Israel, and of the cross in advance. Jesus ends it with the Psalm: the stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner. The Catechism says the Lord compared himself to that stone, and that the Church is built on him. Lent invites us to be built on what the world rejected.

scripture.text: Jesus saith to them: Have you never read in the Scriptures: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner? By the Lord this has been done; and it is wonderful in our eyes.

saint.name: St. Francis of Assisi
saint.reference: Admonitions 5, 3, as quoted in CCC 598
saint.text: Nor did demons crucify him; it is you who have crucified him and crucify him still, when you delight in your vices and sins.

levels.title: While He Was Yet Far Off
levels.reflection: The younger son has spent everything, and the first thing he decides is to rise and go to his father. He rehearses a speech of repentance: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before thee. He never gets to finish it. While he is yet a great way off, his father sees him and is moved with compassion, runs to him, falls on his neck and kisses him. The robe, the ring and the feast follow. The Catechism calls this parable the description of conversion itself, and it says that only the heart of Christ could reveal to us the abyss of his Father's mercy so simply.

scripture.text: And rising up he came to his father. And when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and running to him fell upon his neck, and kissed him.

saint.name: St. Ambrose
saint.reference: On the Sacraments 5, 4, 19, as quoted in CCC 2783
saint.text: O man, you did not dare to raise your face to heaven, you lowered your eyes to the earth, and suddenly you have received the grace of Christ all your sins have been forgiven. From being a wicked servant you have become a good son.

levels.title: A Spring of Water
levels.reflection: In the third week of Lent the Church sits down at a well in Samaria at midday. Jesus, wearied with his journey, asks a woman for a drink, and the conversation turns to a thirst she did not know she had. If you knew the gift of God, he says, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water. The water he gives becomes a fountain springing up into life everlasting. The Catechism says prayer is the meeting of two thirsts: God thirsts that we may thirst for him. Lent is a time to let that thirst be named, and met.

scripture.text: But the water that I will give him, shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting.

levels.title: Seven Times in the Jordan
levels.reflection: Naaman, the commander of the Syrian army, came to Israel with a leprosy no doctor could cure, and was told by the prophet Elisha to wash seven times in the Jordan. It seemed too small a thing, but he went down and washed as the man of God had said, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child. Jesus, in the synagogue at Nazareth, recalls Naaman and warns that no prophet is accepted in his own country, and his townsmen are so enraged that they try to throw him from the hill. God's cures arrive in ordinary water and ordinary obedience. The Church sees in the Jordan a shadow of her Baptism.

scripture.text: Then he went down, and washed in the Jordan seven times: according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored, like the flesh of a little child, and he was made clean.

saint.name: St. Gregory of Nazianzus
saint.reference: Oration 40, 3-4, as quoted in CCC 1216
saint.text: Baptism is God's most beautiful and magnificent gift....We call it gift, grace, anointing, enlightenment, garment of immortality, bath of rebirth, seal, and most precious gift.

levels.title: Seventy Times Seven
levels.reflection: Peter thinks he is being generous when he asks if he should forgive his brother until seven times. Jesus answers: not seven times, but till seventy times seven. Then he tells of a servant who was forgiven a huge debt and then seized his fellow servant over a small one. The lord calls him wicked: should you not have had compassion, as I had compassion on you? The Catechism says this parable crowns the Lord's teaching on ecclesial communion, and that the heart offered to the Holy Spirit turns injury into compassion. Lent does not ask us to forget a wrong. It asks us to hand it over.

scripture.text: Then came Peter unto him and said: Lord, how often shall my brother offend against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith to him: I say not to thee, till seven times; but till seventy times seven times.

levels.title: Not to Destroy, but to Fulfill
levels.reflection: Someone listening to the Sermon on the Mount might think Jesus has come to sweep away the Law. He says the opposite: I am not come to destroy the law or the prophets, but to fulfill. Whoever keeps and teaches even the least of the commandments shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven. Moses had told Israel to keep the words their eyes had seen, and to teach them to their children and grandchildren. The Catechism teaches that the New Law uses the Sermon on the Mount to show us what to do, and the sacraments to give us the grace to do it. Lent is obedience with the strength of grace behind it.

scripture.text: Do not think that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets. I am not come to destroy, but to fulfill.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Sermon on the Mount 1, 1, as quoted in CCC 1966
saint.text: If anyone should meditate with devotion and perspicacity on the sermon our Lord gave on the mount, as we read in the Gospel of Saint Matthew, he will doubtless find there . . . the perfect way of the Christian life.

levels.title: The Finger of God
levels.reflection: Jesus casts out a demon, and some say he does it by the prince of devils. He answers plainly: if I by the finger of God cast out devils, doubtless the kingdom of God is come upon you. The Catechism teaches that the coming of God's kingdom means the defeat of Satan's, and that Jesus' exorcisms anticipate his great victory on the cross. There is no neutral ground: he that is not with me is against me. Jeremiah heard the same appeal long before, when the Lord asked only that Israel hearken to his voice, and he would be their God. Lent is a time to choose a side once more.

scripture.text: But if I by the finger of God cast out devils; doubtless the kingdom of God is come upon you.

saint.name: St. Cyprian
saint.reference: On the Lord's Prayer 13, as quoted in CCC 2816
saint.text: It may even be . . . that the Kingdom of God means Christ himself, whom we daily desire to come, and whose coming we wish to be manifested quickly to us. For as he is our resurrection, since in him we rise, so he can also be understood as the Kingdom of God, for in him we shall reign.

levels.title: The First Commandment
levels.reflection: A scribe asks Jesus which commandment is first of all, and the answer gathers the whole Law into two sentences: love the Lord your God with your whole heart, soul, mind and strength, and love your neighbor as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these. The scribe agrees, and Jesus tells him he is not far from the kingdom of God. Hosea calls Israel back in the same spirit: return to the Lord your God. The Catechism says the Decalogue must be read in the light of this twofold and single commandment of love. Lent's fasting and almsgiving are only love, in two directions.

scripture.text: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God, with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole mind, and with thy whole strength. This is the first commandment. And the second is like to it: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is no other commandment greater than these.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: On the Morals of the Catholic Church 1, 25, 46, as quoted in CCC 1809
saint.text: To live well is nothing other than to love God with all one's heart, with all one's soul and with all one's efforts.

levels.title: Mercy, Not Sacrifice
levels.reflection: Hosea puts it in one line: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than holocausts. Jesus shows what it looks like in a parable of two men who went up to the Temple to pray. The Pharisee stood and thanked God that he was not like other men. The publican stood afar off, would not lift his eyes, struck his breast and said: O God, be merciful to me a sinner. Jesus says it was the publican who went home justified. The Catechism calls asking forgiveness the first movement of the prayer of petition, and the Church still prays this prayer in the Kyrie.

scripture.text: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice: and the knowledge of God more than holocausts.

levels.title: One Thing I Know
levels.reflection: The fourth Sunday of Lent, which the Church has long called Laetare, may bring rose-colored vestments, and this week the Church reads the Gospel of a man blind from his birth. The disciples ask whose sin caused it, and Jesus answers that it was so that the works of God might be made manifest in him. He says he is the light of the world, anoints the man's eyes with clay and sends him to wash. Questioned by the authorities, the man answers: one thing I know, that whereas I was blind, now I see. At the end he believes and adores. The Church calls Baptism enlightenment, because we are brought out of darkness into his light.

scripture.text: He said therefore to them: If he be a sinner, I know not: one thing I know, that whereas I was blind, now I see.

saint.name: St. Irenaeus
saint.reference: Against Heresies 4, 20, 5, as quoted in CCC 1722
saint.text: It is true, because of the greatness and inexpressible glory of God, that "man shall not see me and live," for the Father cannot be grasped. But because of God's love and goodness toward us, and because he can do all things, he goes so far as to grant those who love him the privilege of seeing him.

levels.title: Go Thy Way
levels.reflection: A royal official comes to Jesus because his son is dying, and asks him to come down before the boy dies. Jesus does not go with him. He says only: go thy way; thy son liveth. The man believed the word which Jesus said to him, and went his way, and learned on the road that the fever had left the boy at the very hour Jesus spoke. The whole household came to believe. Faith here is not seeing first. It is walking home on a promise. The Catechism teaches that faith is an entirely free gift of God, and Isaiah's promise of new heavens and a new earth is the same hope.

scripture.text: Jesus saith to him: Go thy way; thy son liveth. The man believed the word which Jesus said to him, and went his way.

levels.title: Water from the Temple
levels.reflection: Ezekiel sees water flowing out from under the threshold of the Temple, eastward, deepening into a river. Wherever it goes, everything lives. In the Gospel, a man lies by the pool of Bethsaida who has been sick thirty-eight years, and Jesus asks him: wilt thou be made whole? He tells him to rise, take up his bed and walk, and the man is made whole at once. Afterwards Jesus finds him in the Temple and warns him to sin no more. The Church hears in both the waters of Baptism, which the Catechism calls the gateway to life in the Spirit.

scripture.text: And every living creature that creepeth whithersoever the torrent shall come, shall live: and there shall be fishes in abundance after these waters shall come thither, and they shall be healed, and all things shall live to which the torrent shall come.

saint.name: St. Irenaeus
saint.reference: Demonstration of the Apostolic Preaching 7, as quoted in CCC 683
saint.text: Baptism gives us the grace of new birth in God the Father, through his Son, in the Holy Spirit. For those who bear God's Spirit are led to the Word, that is, to the Son, and the Son presents them to the Father, and the Father confers incorruptibility on them.

levels.title: Graven on His Hands
levels.reflection: When Zion cries that the Lord has forgotten her, Isaiah answers with a picture few people can bear to look at straight. Can a woman forget her infant, so as not to have pity on the son of her womb? Yes, perhaps, and yet I will not forget thee, says the Lord. He has graven us on his hands. The Catechism teaches that God's parental tenderness can also be expressed by the image of motherhood, even as it adds that he transcends the human distinction between the sexes. St. Catherine of Siena puts the whole of Lent in a line: everything comes from love. The ashes of this season mark a people who are remembered.

scripture.text: Can a woman forget her infant, so as not to have pity on the son of her womb? and if she should forget, yet will not I forget thee.

saint.name: St. Catherine of Siena
saint.reference: Dialogue 4, 138, as quoted in CCC 313
saint.text: Everything comes from love, all is ordained for the salvation of man, God does nothing without this goal in mind.

levels.title: Moses Besought the Lord
levels.reflection: While Moses is on the mountain, the people make a golden calf, and the Lord tells him that he will destroy them. Moses does not argue that they deserve better. He pleads that these are the people the Lord brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand, and the Lord was appeased from doing the evil he had spoken. The Catechism calls the prayer of Moses the most striking example of intercessory prayer, one that finds its fulfillment in the one mediator between God and men. In Lent we are all asked to stand in the gap for someone. You do not need to be Moses to do so.

scripture.text: But Moses besought the Lord his God, saying: Why, O Lord, is thy indignation kindled against thy people, whom thou hast brought out of the land of Egypt, with great power, and with a mighty hand?

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Commentary on Psalm 85, 1, as quoted in CCC 2616
saint.text: He prays for us as our priest, prays in us as our Head, and is prayed to by us as our God. Therefore let us acknowledge our voice in him and his in us.

levels.title: The Just Man Is Not for Our Turn
levels.reflection: The Book of Wisdom records what the wicked say among themselves: let us lie in wait for the just, because he is contrary to our doings and upbraids us. If he is the true son of God, he will defend him. Let us condemn him to a most shameful death. The Church has always read these words in the light of the Passion. The Catechism reminds us that sinners were the authors and the ministers of all the sufferings that the divine Redeemer endured, so that no one stands outside the story. The early Christians honored martyrs as the Lord's disciples and imitators, and so should we.

scripture.text: For if he be the true son of God, he will defend him, and will deliver him from the hands of his enemies.

saint.name: Martyrdom of Polycarp
saint.reference: Martyrium Polycarpi 17, as quoted in CCC 957
saint.text: We worship Christ as God's Son; we love the martyrs as the Lord's disciples and imitators, and rightly so because of their matchless devotion towards their king and master. May we also be their companions and fellow disciples!

levels.title: Never Did Man Speak Like This
levels.reflection: The chief priests send officers to arrest Jesus, and they come back empty-handed. When asked why they did not bring him, they can only say: never did man speak like this man. The crowd is divided because of him, and the leaders cannot agree. Jeremiah foretold this loneliness long before: I was as a meek lamb that is carried to be a victim, and I knew not that they had devised counsels against me. The Catechism quotes St. John of the Cross that in giving us his Son, God spoke everything at once in this sole Word. Lent is a time for listening to that one Word.

scripture.text: The ministers answered: Never did man speak like this man.

saint.name: St. John of the Cross
saint.reference: Ascent of Mount Carmel 2, 22, 3-5, as quoted in CCC 65
saint.text: In giving us his Son, his only Word (for he possesses no other), he spoke everything to us at once in this sole Word - and he has no more to say.

levels.title: I Am the Resurrection
levels.reflection: In the fifth week of Lent the Church goes to Bethany, to a tomb where a man has lain four days. Martha meets Jesus on the road and says what many have said at a graveside: if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. He answers with a claim only God can make: I am the resurrection and the life; he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live. Then Jesus wept. He stands at the tomb, cries with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth, and the dead man walks out in his winding bands. The Catechism says this is a pledge of his own Resurrection, and the Eucharist already gives us a foretaste of ours.

scripture.text: Jesus said to her: I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live: And every one that liveth, and believeth in me, shall not die for ever. Believest thou this?

saint.name: St. Irenaeus
saint.reference: Against Heresies 4, 18, 4-5, as quoted in CCC 1000
saint.text: Just as bread that comes from the earth, after God's blessing has been invoked upon it, is no longer ordinary bread, but Eucharist, formed of two things, the one earthly and the other heavenly: so too our bodies, which partake of the Eucharist, are no longer corruptible, but possess the hope of resurrection.

levels.title: Neither Will I Condemn Thee
levels.reflection: They bring Jesus a woman caught in adultery and set her in the midst. The Law, they say, commands that such a woman be stoned, and they wait to see what he will say. He stoops and writes on the ground, and when they press him he says: he that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her. One by one they leave, the eldest first. Jesus is left alone with the woman: has no man condemned thee? No man, Lord. Neither will I condemn thee; go, and now sin no more. He does not excuse the sin, and he does not crush the sinner. The Catechism calls the Gospel the revelation of God's mercy to sinners.

scripture.text: Who said: No man, Lord. And Jesus said: Neither will I condemn thee. Go, and now sin no more.

saint.name: St. Ignatius of Loyola
saint.reference: Spiritual Exercises 22, as quoted in CCC 2478
saint.text: Every good Christian ought to be more ready to give a favorable interpretation to another's statement than to condemn it.

levels.title: Lifted Up
levels.reflection: In the desert the people were bitten by serpents and cried out for help, and the Lord told Moses to make a bronze serpent and set it on a pole: whoever looks on it shall live. Jesus applies the image to himself. As Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have life everlasting. And when you have lifted up the Son of man, he says, then you shall know that I am he. The Catechism notes that God had already ordained the bronze serpent as a sign pointing toward salvation by the incarnate Word. The cross is where the healing is.

scripture.text: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him, may not perish; but may have life everlasting.

saint.name: St. Ambrose
saint.reference: On the Sacraments 2, 2, 6, as quoted in CCC 1225
saint.text: See where you are baptized, see where Baptism comes from, if not from the cross of Christ, from his death. There is the whole mystery: he died for you. In him you are redeemed, in him you are saved.

levels.title: The Truth Shall Make You Free
levels.reflection: Jesus speaks to Jews who believed him, and promises them freedom on one condition: if you continue in my word, you shall be my disciples indeed, and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. They object that they have never been slaves, and he answers that whoever commits sin is the servant of sin. Real freedom is not doing what one likes. The Catechism teaches that the more one does what is good the freer one becomes, and that the choice to do evil is an abuse of freedom that leads to the slavery of sin. Lent is a school of freedom, one small refusal at a time.

scripture.text: Then Jesus said to those Jews, who believed him: If you continue in my word, you shall be my disciples indeed. And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

saint.name: Origen
saint.reference: Homilies on Exodus 8, 1, as quoted in CCC 2061
saint.text: Since there was a passing from the paradise of freedom to the slavery of this world, in punishment for sin, the first phrase of the Decalogue, the first word of God's commandments, bears on freedom.

levels.title: Before Abraham Was
levels.reflection: The Lord changes Abram's name to Abraham, because he has made him a father of many nations. In the Gospel Jesus tells his opponents that Abraham rejoiced that he might see his day, and that he saw it and was glad. They are astonished: thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham? And he answers: before Abraham was made, I am. They take up stones, for they understand exactly what he claims. The Catechism says that only the divine identity of Jesus' person can justify so absolute a claim, and puts that saying beside I and the Father are one. In Lent we are asked to look at who is speaking.

scripture.text: Jesus said to them: Amen, amen I say to you, before Abraham was made, I am.

levels.title: A Strong Warrior
levels.reflection: Jeremiah is whispered about and watched for a slip. Every friend waits for his fall, and he knows what they plan for him. And yet he says: the Lord is with me as a strong warrior. In the Gospel the crowd takes up stones against Jesus, because he said: I and the Father are one. He answers them with his works: if you will not believe me, believe the works, that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I in the Father. Jeremiah trusts in the Lord, and Jesus rests in the Father. The Catechism calls martyrdom the supreme witness to the truth of the faith, and St. Ignatius of Antioch goes to it singing.

scripture.text: But the Lord is with me as a strong warrior: therefore they that persecute me shall fall, and shall be weak: they shall be greatly confounded, because they have not understood the everlasting reproach, which never shall be effaced.

saint.name: St. Ignatius of Antioch
saint.reference: Letter to the Romans 6, 1-2, as quoted in CCC 2474
saint.text: It is better for me to die [in order to unite myself] to Christ Jesus than to reign over the ends of the earth. I seek him who died for us; I desire him who rose for us.

levels.title: One Man for the People
levels.reflection: After Lazarus is raised, the chief priests and Pharisees gather the council. If we let him alone, they say, all will believe in him. Caiaphas, the high priest that year, says what he does not understand: it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not. John adds that he did not say this of himself. He prophesied, and Jesus was to die not only for the nation, but to gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed. Ezekiel had promised a covenant of peace, an everlasting covenant. The plot against the Lord's life becomes the means of our redemption.

scripture.text: Neither do you consider that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.

saint.name: St. Ambrose
saint.reference: On the Sacraments 4, 6, 28, as quoted in CCC 1393
saint.text: If we proclaim the Lord's death, we proclaim the forgiveness of sins.

levels.title: Hosanna to the Son of David
levels.reflection: Palm Sunday begins with a procession, branches, and a donkey. The crowd goes before Jesus and after him, crying: Hosanna, blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord. And then the Church reads the Passion. The Catechism says that Jesus chose the time and prepared the details of his entry, and that he conquers Jerusalem neither by ruse nor by violence but by the humility that bears witness to the truth. St. Paul sums up the week in a hymn: he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross, and for that cause God also hath exalted him. We enter Holy Week by walking behind the one who rides ahead.

scripture.text: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross. For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names:

saint.name: St. John Eudes
saint.reference: Liturgy of the Hours, week 33, Friday, Office of Readings, as quoted in CCC 521
saint.text: We must continue to accomplish in ourselves the stages of Jesus' life and his mysteries and often to beg him to perfect and realize them in us and in his whole Church.

levels.title: A Pound of Spikenard
levels.reflection: Six days before the Passover Jesus comes to Bethany, to the house of Lazarus whom he raised from the dead. Mary takes a pound of costly ointment, anoints his feet and wipes them with her hair, and the whole house is filled with the fragrance. Judas complains that it might have been sold for the poor. Jesus answers: the poor you have always with you; but me you have not always. Isaiah gives the servant's quiet portrait for the same Monday: the bruised reed he shall not break. The Catechism teaches that it is by what they have done for the poor that Jesus Christ will recognize his chosen ones. Love for the poor and love lavished on Christ are one love.

scripture.text: Mary therefore took a pound of ointment of right spikenard, of great price, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment.

levels.title: And It Was Night
levels.reflection: At the Last Supper Jesus is troubled in spirit and says plainly: one of you shall betray me. He gives the morsel to Judas, and Judas goes out immediately. John adds three words: and it was night. Jesus then tells Peter that before the cock crows he will deny him three times. Isaiah's servant is called for more than Israel: it is a small thing to raise up the tribes of Jacob, he is given as a light to the Gentiles that the Lord's salvation may reach the farthest part of the earth. The Catechism recalls how Peter's tears came: Jesus' look of infinite mercy drew tears of repentance, and then a threefold affirmation of love.

scripture.text: He therefore having received the morsel, went out immediately. And it was night.

levels.title: I Have Not Turned Away
levels.reflection: On Wednesday of Holy Week the Church places two voices side by side. Isaiah's servant says: I have given my body to the strikers, and my cheeks to them that plucked them; I have not turned away my face from them that rebuked me. The Lord God is my helper, therefore am I not confounded. In the Gospel Judas goes to the chief priests and asks: what will you give me, and I will deliver him unto you? They appoint him thirty pieces of silver. At the supper, when Jesus says one of the Twelve will betray him, Judas asks: is it I, Rabbi? Tomorrow evening the Triduum begins. The days of Lent were meant to bring us here.

scripture.text: I have given my body to the strikers, and my cheeks to them that plucked them: I have not turned away my face from them that rebuked me, and spit upon me.

questions.prompt: In Joel 2:13, what does the prophet tell Israel to rend?
choices: Their hearts, and not their garments
Their garments, as a sign of mourning
Their bonds, and let the debtors go free
Their idols, and cast them from the land
questions.correctAnswer: Their hearts, and not their garments
questions.explanation: The Douay-Rheims reads: "And rend your hearts, and not your garments." The outward sign of grief is worth nothing without the change of heart.

questions.prompt: Joel says the Lord is gracious and merciful, patient and rich in ____.
questions.explanation: Joel 2:13 says the Lord is "gracious and merciful, patient and rich in mercy."

questions.prompt: True or False: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus tells his disciples to look sad when they fast, so that others will see it.
questions.explanation: Jesus says the opposite: "when you fast, be not as the hypocrites, sad." The disciple fasts for the Father who sees in secret.

questions.prompt: Which three forms of penance does the Catechism say Scripture and the Fathers insist on above all?
choices: Confession, vigil, and sacrifice
Poverty, chastity, and obedience
Fasting, prayer, and almsgiving
Pilgrimage, silence, and study
questions.explanation: The Catechism says Scripture and the Fathers insist above all on fasting, prayer and almsgiving, which express conversion in relation to oneself, to God and to others.

questions.prompt: In Deuteronomy 30:19, what two pairs does Moses say he has set before Israel?
choices: Peace and war, plenty and famine
Life and death, blessing and cursing
Light and darkness, day and night
Wisdom and folly, riches and poverty
questions.correctAnswer: Life and death, blessing and cursing
questions.explanation: Moses says: "I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing. Choose therefore life."

questions.prompt: Moses says, "Choose therefore ____, that both thou and thy seed may live."
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 30:19 reads: "Choose therefore life, that both thou and thy seed may live."

questions.prompt: In Luke 9:23, what does Jesus say anyone must do who will come after him?
choices: Pray in the Temple and give alms
Fast and keep the whole Law of Moses
Deny himself and take up his cross daily
Leave his family and sell all his goods
questions.correctAnswer: Deny himself and take up his cross daily
questions.explanation: Jesus says to all: "If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism calls taking up one's cross each day and following Jesus the easiest way of penance.
questions.explanation: Catechism 1435 calls it not the easiest but "the surest way of penance."

questions.prompt: According to Isaiah 58:7, what does the fast the Lord has chosen include?
choices: Dealing bread to the hungry and sheltering the needy
Keeping silence from the rising of the sun to its setting
Offering the firstlings of the flock on the altar
Praying aloud in the gates of the city each morning
questions.correctAnswer: Dealing bread to the hungry and sheltering the needy
questions.explanation: Isaiah says: "Deal thy bread to the hungry, and bring the needy and the harbourless into thy house."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Isaiah 58, the Lord says the fast he has chosen is to keep silence and abstain from bread.
questions.explanation: The Lord says the fast he has chosen is to "loose the bands of wickedness, undo the bundles that oppress."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 9:15, why does Jesus say his disciples do not fast while he is with them?
choices: The Sabbath forbids fasting
The Law no longer binds them
They are not yet baptized
The bridegroom is with them
questions.explanation: Jesus asks: "Can the children of the bridegroom mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them?" When he is taken away, then they shall fast.

questions.prompt: Which days does the Catechism name as the Church's seasons and days of penance in the liturgical year?
choices: Lent, and each Sunday in memory of the Resurrection
Advent, and each Saturday in honor of Our Lady
Ordinary Time, and every Wednesday of the year
Lent, and each Friday in memory of the Lord's death
questions.correctAnswer: Lent, and each Friday in memory of the Lord's death
questions.explanation: The Catechism names Lent, and each Friday in memory of the death of the Lord, as intense moments of the Church's penitential practice.

questions.prompt: What did Jesus say to the publican Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom?
choices: Sell what thou hast
Come and see
Leave thy nets
Follow me
questions.explanation: Luke tells us that Jesus "saw a publican named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom, and he said to him: Follow me."

questions.prompt: In Luke 5:30, who murmured that Jesus' disciples ate and drank with publicans and sinners?
choices: The disciples of John
The Sadducees and Herodians
The Pharisees and scribes
The chief priests and elders
questions.explanation: Luke writes: "the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying to his disciples: Why do you eat and drink with publicans and sinners?"

questions.prompt: Jesus says, "I came not to call the just, but sinners to ____."
questions.explanation: In the Douay-Rheims Jesus says: "I came not to call the just, but sinners to penance."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says the Church, clasping sinners to her bosom, is at once holy and always in need of purification.
questions.explanation: Catechism 1428 says the Church, "clasping sinners to her bosom," is at once holy and always in need of purification, and follows constantly the path of penance and renewal.

questions.prompt: How long does Matthew say Jesus fasted in the desert before he was hungry?
choices: Forty days and forty nights
Seven days and seven nights
Three days and three nights
Twelve days and twelve nights
questions.explanation: Matthew writes: "when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, afterwards he was hungry."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus answer when the tempter tells him to make the stones bread?
choices: Man lives not by bread alone, but by every word from God
Man shall eat his bread in the sweat of his face
Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us
The bread of heaven is better than the bread of earth
questions.correctAnswer: Man lives not by bread alone, but by every word from God
questions.explanation: Jesus answers from Scripture: "Not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word that proceedeth from the mouth of God."

questions.prompt: When the devil sets Jesus on the pinnacle of the Temple and tells him to cast himself down, how does Jesus answer?
choices: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart
Remember that thou keep holy the sabbath day
Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord in vain
Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
questions.correctAnswer: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
questions.explanation: Jesus said to him: "It is written again: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, by the solemn forty days of Lent the Church unites herself each year to what?
choices: The agony of Jesus in the garden
The transfiguration of Jesus on the mountain
The finding of Jesus in the Temple
The mystery of Jesus in the desert
questions.correctAnswer: The mystery of Jesus in the desert
questions.explanation: Catechism 540 says that by the solemn forty days of Lent the Church "unites herself each year to the mystery of Jesus in the desert."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 25, what does the king say he was when those on his right gave him to eat?
choices: Sick
A stranger
In prison
Hungry
questions.explanation: The king says: "I was hungry, and you gave me to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me to drink."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Matthew 25, the king says that what was done for the least of his brethren was done for him.
questions.explanation: The king says: "as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me."

questions.prompt: Leviticus 19:18 commands: "Thou shalt love thy friend as ____."
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:18 reads: "Thou shalt love thy friend as thyself." The Church reads it on the same day as the judgment of Matthew 25.

questions.prompt: What does the Catechism call one of the chief witnesses to fraternal charity?
choices: Praying the Stations of the Cross
Giving alms to the poor
Fasting on the Fridays of Lent
Attending Mass each day
questions.explanation: Catechism 2447 says: "giving alms to the poor is one of the chief witnesses to fraternal charity: it is also a work of justice pleasing to God."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 6:7, whom does Jesus say his disciples should not imitate when they pray?
choices: The publicans, who beat their breasts afar off
The heathens, who think they are heard for their much speaking
The scribes, who make long prayers for a pretence
The Pharisees, who pray standing in the synagogues
questions.correctAnswer: The heathens, who think they are heard for their much speaking
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "when you are praying, speak not much, as the heathens. For they think that in their much speaking they may be heard."

questions.prompt: In the Lord's Prayer we say: "And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our ____."
questions.explanation: The Douay-Rheims reads: "And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors."

questions.prompt: True or False: Through Isaiah the Lord says that his word will return to him void.
questions.explanation: The Lord says the opposite: "it shall not return to me void, but it shall do whatsoever I please."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, how did liturgical usage very early on conclude the Lord's Prayer?
choices: With a blessing of the people
With a doxology
With a psalm
With the sign of the cross
questions.explanation: Catechism 2760 says that very early on, liturgical usage concluded the Lord's Prayer with a doxology. The Didache has: "For yours are the power and the glory for ever."

questions.prompt: In Jonah 3:5, what did the men of Nineveh do when they believed in God?
choices: They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth
They drove Jonah out of the city gates
They built an altar and offered the firstlings
They sent gifts to the prophet to end his warning
questions.correctAnswer: They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth
questions.explanation: Jonah says: "the men of Ninive believed in God: and they proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least."

questions.prompt: True or False: When God saw that the people of Nineveh had turned from their evil way, he destroyed the city as he had threatened.
questions.explanation: Scripture says: "God saw their works, that they were turned from their evil way: and God had mercy."

questions.prompt: In Luke 11:29, what sign does Jesus say will be given to this wicked generation?
choices: The sign of the rainbow
The sign of the bronze serpent
The sign of Elijah the prophet
The sign of Jonah the prophet
questions.correctAnswer: The sign of Jonah the prophet
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "This generation is a wicked generation: it asketh a sign, and a sign shall not be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet."

questions.prompt: Jesus says the men of Nineveh "did ____ at the preaching of Jonas."
questions.explanation: Luke 11:32 says of the men of Nineveh: "they did penance at the preaching of Jonas; and behold more than Jonas here."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find: ____, and it shall be opened to you."
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:7 reads: "Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 7:11, how does Jesus show that the Father will give good things to those who ask him?
choices: If evil parents give good gifts to their children, how much more will the Father
Because the angels carry each prayer to his throne
Because those who fast have earned an answer from him
Because the Law commands him to answer every prayer
questions.correctAnswer: If evil parents give good gifts to their children, how much more will the Father
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "If you then being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children: how much more will your Father who is in heaven, give good things to them that ask him?"

questions.prompt: True or False: According to Matthew 7:8, to the one who knocks it shall be opened.
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shall be opened."

questions.prompt: How does the Catechism, quoting St. John Damascene, describe prayer?
choices: The offering of fasting and almsgiving
The raising of one's mind and heart to God
A duty owed to God under the Law
The recitation of the psalms in the Temple
questions.correctAnswer: The raising of one's mind and heart to God
questions.explanation: Catechism 2559 says: "Prayer is the raising of one's mind and heart to God or the requesting of good things from God." It adds that humility is the foundation of prayer.

questions.prompt: In Ezekiel 18:23, what does the Lord say is not his will?
choices: That Israel should keep the feasts without the sacrifices
That the poor should be left without a defender
That the prophets should speak in his name
That a sinner should die rather than be converted and live
questions.correctAnswer: That a sinner should die rather than be converted and live
questions.explanation: The Lord asks: "Is it my will that a sinner should die, saith the Lord God, and not that he should be converted from his ways, and live?"

questions.prompt: True or False: According to Ezekiel, when the wicked man turns away from his wickedness and does judgment and justice, he shall save his soul alive.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel says: "when the wicked turneth himself away from his wickedness, which he hath wrought, and doeth judgment, and justice: he shall save his soul alive."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 5:23-24, what does Jesus tell a man who remembers at the altar that his brother has something against him?
choices: Offer a second sacrifice for the wrong he has done
Leave his offering and go first to be reconciled to his brother
Wait until the feast has ended before he speaks
Finish his offering and then ask his brother's pardon
questions.correctAnswer: Leave his offering and go first to be reconciled to his brother
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "Leave there thy offering before the altar, and go first to be reconciled to thy brother: and then coming thou shalt offer thy gift."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, why is the sacrament called the sacrament of conversion?
choices: It must be received once in a lifetime before death
It makes sacramentally present Jesus' call to conversion
It is the first sacrament given to children
It restores the baptismal garment to the dying
questions.correctAnswer: It makes sacramentally present Jesus' call to conversion
questions.explanation: Catechism 1423 says it is called the sacrament of conversion because it makes sacramentally present Jesus' call to conversion, the first step in returning to the Father from whom one has strayed by sin.

questions.prompt: Jesus says in the Sermon on the Mount: "Love your ____: do good to them that hate you."
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:44 reads: "Love your enemies: do good to them that hate you: and pray for them that persecute and calumniate you."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 5:45, what does Jesus say the Father does for the good and the bad, the just and the unjust?
choices: Makes his sun rise and sends rain on them all
Gives them each a share of the harvest
Judges them alike on the last day
Hears their prayers and forgives their sins
questions.correctAnswer: Makes his sun rise and sends rain on them all
questions.explanation: Jesus says the Father "maketh his sun to rise upon the good, and bad, and raineth upon the just and the unjust."

questions.prompt: How does Matthew 5:48 end the Lord's teaching on love of enemies?
choices: Be you therefore merciful, as your brethren are merciful
Be you therefore perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect
Be you therefore watchful, as the servants are watchful
Be you therefore wise, as the serpents are wise
questions.correctAnswer: Be you therefore perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect
questions.explanation: Jesus concludes: "Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says that Christ died out of love for us only after we had repented of our sins.
questions.explanation: Catechism 1825 says Christ died out of love for us while we were still "enemies," and asks us to love as he does, even our enemies.

questions.prompt: In Mark 9, which three disciples does Jesus take with him up the high mountain?
choices: Peter, James and John
Peter, John and Matthew
James, John and Thomas
Peter, Andrew and Philip
questions.explanation: Mark writes: "Jesus taketh with him Peter and James and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves, and was transfigured before them."

questions.prompt: What does the voice from the cloud say in Mark 9?
choices: Go down and tell no man what thou hast seen
This is my servant, in whom my soul delighteth
This is my most beloved son; hear ye him
Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee
questions.correctAnswer: This is my most beloved son; hear ye him
questions.explanation: Mark says: "a voice came out of the cloud, saying: This is my most beloved son; hear ye him."

questions.prompt: In Genesis 22:12, what does the angel tell Abraham as he raises his hand to offer his son?
choices: Offer the ram in his place at once
Go back down the mountain in peace
Lay not thy hand upon the boy
Take thy son and flee from the land
questions.correctAnswer: Lay not thy hand upon the boy
questions.explanation: The angel says: "Lay not thy hand upon the boy, neither do thou any thing to him: now I know that thou fearest God."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, of what did Moses and Elijah speak with Jesus at the Transfiguration?
choices: His departure, which he was to accomplish at Jerusalem
The disciples who would soon betray him
The kingdom he would restore to Israel
The temple he would build in three days
questions.correctAnswer: His departure, which he was to accomplish at Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Catechism 554 says Moses and Elijah appear, speaking "of his departure, which he was to accomplish at Jerusalem."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "Be ye therefore merciful, as your ____ also is merciful."
questions.explanation: Luke 6:36 reads: "Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful."

questions.prompt: According to Luke 6:37, what does Jesus promise to those who forgive?
choices: They shall see the face of God
They shall be forgiven
They shall be called the children of God
They shall inherit the earth
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "Judge not, and you shall not be judged. Condemn not, and you shall not be condemned. Forgive, and you shall be forgiven."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says that confession of everyday faults is forbidden by the Church.
questions.explanation: Catechism 1458 says confession of everyday faults (venial sins) is "nevertheless strongly recommended by the Church."

questions.prompt: Which of these does the Catechism list among the spiritual works of mercy?
choices: Forgiving and bearing wrongs patiently
Burying the dead
Visiting the imprisoned
Feeding the hungry
questions.explanation: Catechism 2447 says: "Instructing, advising, consoling, comforting are spiritual works of mercy, as are forgiving and bearing wrongs patiently." Burying the dead, visiting the imprisoned and feeding the hungry are corporal works.

questions.prompt: In Isaiah 1:18, what does the Lord promise to sins that are as scarlet?
choices: They shall be covered by the blood of the lamb
They shall be remembered no more by men
They shall be carried away on the scapegoat
They shall be made as white as snow
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be made as white as snow
questions.explanation: The Lord says: "if your sins be as scarlet, they shall be made as white as snow: and if they be red as crimson, they shall be white as wool."

questions.prompt: The Lord says through Isaiah: "Wash yourselves, be ____, take away the evil of your devices from my eyes."
questions.explanation: Isaiah 1:16 reads: "Wash yourselves, be clean, take away the evil of your devices from my eyes: cease to do perversely."

questions.prompt: According to Matthew 23:12, what happens to whoever humbles himself?
choices: He shall be forgotten
He shall be called the least
He shall be sent away empty
He shall be exalted
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "whosoever shall exalt himself shall be humbled: and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the Word call voluntary humility?
choices: Poverty of the flesh
The fear of the Lord
Poverty in spirit
Meekness of heart
questions.explanation: Catechism 2546 says the Word speaks of voluntary humility as "poverty in spirit."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 20:22, what does Jesus ask James and John whether they can drink?
choices: The cup of the wedding at Cana
The new wine of the kingdom
The waters of the Jordan
The chalice that he shall drink
questions.correctAnswer: The chalice that he shall drink
questions.explanation: Jesus asks: "You know not what you ask. Can you drink the chalice that I shall drink?" They say to him: "We can."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 20:28, the Son of man has come to minister and to give his life as what?
choices: A sacrifice for Israel
A redemption for many
A light for the Gentiles
A witness to the nations
questions.explanation: Jesus says the Son of man "is not come to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a redemption for many."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Matthew 20, Jesus says whoever would be the greater among his disciples must be their minister.
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "whosoever will be the greater among you, let him be your minister."

questions.prompt: How does the Catechism, quoting Jesus, sum up Christ's whole mission?
choices: To heal the sick and cast out unclean spirits
To teach the Law to all nations and be their light
To judge the living and the dead and restore Israel
To serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many
questions.correctAnswer: To serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many
questions.explanation: Catechism 608 says: "Christ's whole life expresses his mission: 'to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.'"

questions.prompt: In Jeremiah 17:5, whom does the Lord call cursed?
choices: The man that speaks against the king of Judah
The man that trusts in man and makes flesh his arm
The man that hoards grain in a time of famine
The man that rests on the sabbath without prayer
questions.correctAnswer: The man that trusts in man and makes flesh his arm
questions.explanation: The Lord says: "Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord."

questions.prompt: Jeremiah says: "Blessed be the man that trusteth in the ____, and the Lord shall be his confidence."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 17:7 reads: "Blessed be the man that trusteth in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his confidence."

questions.prompt: In the parable of Luke 16, what does Abraham say the rich man's brothers already have?
choices: Moses and the prophets
The Law and the Temple
The word of the apostles
A sign from heaven
questions.explanation: Abraham says: "They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them." If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they believe, if one rise again from the dead.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says that when we attend to the needs of those in want, we give them what is ours, not theirs.
questions.explanation: Catechism 2446 says: "we give them what is theirs, not ours."

questions.prompt: What Scripture does Jesus quote at the end of the parable of the vineyard in Matthew 21:42?
choices: The Lord is my shepherd and I shall want nothing
Out of Egypt have I called my son
The zeal of thy house hath eaten me up
The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner
questions.correctAnswer: The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner? By the Lord this has been done; and it is wonderful in our eyes."

questions.prompt: In the parable of Matthew 21, whom does the householder send to the husbandmen last of all?
choices: His steward
His son
His servants again
His friend
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "last of all he sent to them his son, saying: They will reverence my son."

questions.prompt: In Genesis 37:28, for how many pieces of silver did the brothers sell Joseph?
choices: Ten
Thirty
Twenty
Forty
questions.explanation: Scripture says Joseph's brothers "sold him to the Ismaelites, for twenty pieces of silver: and they led him into Egypt."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says the Lord compared himself to the stone which the builders rejected, and that on this foundation the Church is built.
questions.explanation: Catechism 756 says the Lord compared himself to the stone which the builders rejected, and that on this foundation the Church is built by the apostles.

questions.prompt: In Luke 15:20, what does the father do when he sees his son a great way off?
choices: He is moved with compassion and runs to him and kisses him
He calls his elder son to receive the returning one
He waits at the gate until his son has spoken
He sends his servants to ask what the boy has brought
questions.correctAnswer: He is moved with compassion and runs to him and kisses him
questions.explanation: Luke writes: "his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and running to him fell upon his neck, and kissed him."

questions.prompt: The father says: "This my son was ____, and is come to life again: was lost, and is found."
questions.explanation: Luke 15:24 reads: "Because this my son was dead, and is come to life again: was lost, and is found."

questions.prompt: True or False: The prophet Micah says the Lord will cast all our sins into the fire.
questions.explanation: Micah says of the Lord: "he will cast all our sins into the bottom of the sea."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what do the robe, the ring and the festive banquet in the parable symbolize?
choices: The feasts that Israel keeps each year
The inheritance owed to the elder son
The new life of anyone who returns to God
The gifts of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost
questions.correctAnswer: The new life of anyone who returns to God
questions.explanation: Catechism 1439 says the robe, the ring and the festive banquet are symbols of the new life, pure, worthy and joyful, of anyone who returns to God and to the bosom of his family, which is the Church.

questions.prompt: In John 4:10, what does Jesus say the Samaritan woman would have asked of him if she knew the gift of God?
choices: The forgiveness of her sins
Living water
The bread of life
A sign from heaven
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "If thou didst know the gift of God, and who he is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou perhaps wouldst have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "God is a ____: and they that adore him, must adore him in spirit and in truth."
questions.explanation: John 4:24 reads: "God is a spirit; and they that adore him, must adore him in spirit and in truth."

questions.prompt: According to John 4:14, what does the water that Jesus gives become in the one who drinks it?
choices: A river that flows out to the nations
A well that never needs to be drawn
A cloud that covers the one who prays
A fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting
questions.correctAnswer: A fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "the water that I will give him, shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, prayer is the encounter of what?
choices: God's thirst with ours
Our fasting with God's reward
God's law with our will
Our silence with God's word
questions.explanation: Catechism 2560 says: "prayer is the encounter of God's thirst with ours. God thirsts that we may thirst for him."

questions.prompt: According to 4 Kings 5:14, how many times did Naaman wash in the Jordan?
choices: Twelve
Three
Forty
Seven
questions.explanation: Scripture says Naaman "went down, and washed in the Jordan seven times: according to the word of the man of God."

questions.prompt: True or False: After Naaman washed seven times in the Jordan, his flesh was still leprous.
questions.explanation: Scripture says that "his flesh was restored, like the flesh of a little child, and he was made clean."

questions.prompt: In Luke 4:24, what does Jesus say about a prophet in his own country?
choices: A prophet is sent only to the lost sheep of Israel
A prophet is honored first among his own kin
A prophet must be tested in the desert
No prophet is accepted in his own country
questions.correctAnswer: No prophet is accepted in his own country
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "Amen I say to you, that no prophet is accepted in his own country."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the Greek word baptizein mean?
choices: To anoint or consecrate
To bless or sanctify
To cleanse or purify
To plunge or immerse
questions.explanation: Catechism 1214 says the Greek baptizein means to plunge or immerse, and that the plunge into the water symbolizes the catechumen's burial into Christ's death, from which he rises with him as a new creature.

questions.prompt: When Peter asks if he should forgive his brother until seven times, how does Jesus answer?
choices: Until seven times seven times
Until seventy times seven times
Until the third offence
Until the offender asks pardon
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "I say not to thee, till seven times; but till seventy times seven times."

questions.prompt: In the parable of Matthew 18, what does the lord say to the servant he had forgiven?
choices: Shouldst not thou have had compassion on thy fellow servant, even as I had compassion on thee?
Thou hast been faithful in a little, enter into my joy
Take what is thine and go thy way
Go and sin no more, and pay what thou canst
questions.correctAnswer: Shouldst not thou have had compassion on thy fellow servant, even as I had compassion on thee?
questions.explanation: The lord says: "Thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all the debt, because thou besoughtest me: Shouldst not thou then have had compassion also on thy fellow servant, even as I had compassion on thee?"

questions.prompt: True or False: Jesus ends the parable by saying the heavenly Father will do the same to those who do not forgive their brother from their hearts.
questions.explanation: Jesus concludes: "So also shall my heavenly Father do to you, if you forgive not every one his brother from your hearts."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the heart that offers itself to the Holy Spirit do with an injury?
choices: Leaves the offender to God's judgment
Turns injury into compassion
Hides the wound from others
Forgets the offense entirely
questions.explanation: Catechism 2843 says the heart that offers itself to the Holy Spirit "turns injury into compassion and purifies the memory in transforming the hurt into intercession."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "I am not come to destroy, but to ____."
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:17 reads: "I am not come to destroy, but to fulfill."

questions.prompt: According to Matthew 5:19, what shall he be called who does and teaches the commandments?
choices: The servant of all
A son of peace
The least of the brethren
Great in the kingdom of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Great in the kingdom of heaven
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "he that shall do and teach, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Deuteronomy 4, Moses tells Israel to teach the words they have seen to their sons and their grandsons.
questions.explanation: Moses says: "Forget not the words that thy eyes have seen... Thou shalt teach them to thy sons and to thy grandsons."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the New Law use the Sermon on the Mount to do?
choices: Replace the commandments given to Moses
Teach us what must be done
Excuse the weak from the commandments
Show which works earn heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Teach us what must be done
questions.explanation: Catechism 1966 says the New Law "uses the Sermon on the Mount to teach us what must be done" and makes use of the sacraments to give us the grace to do it.

questions.prompt: In Luke 11:20, what does Jesus say shows that the kingdom of God has come upon his hearers?
choices: That he casts out devils by the finger of God
That the sick are healed at the pool
That the prophets have been sent again
That the Law is read in the synagogue
questions.correctAnswer: That he casts out devils by the finger of God
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "if I by the finger of God cast out devils; doubtless the kingdom of God is come upon you."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Luke 11:23 Jesus says that he who is not with him is neutral.
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "He that is not with me, is against me; and he that gathereth not with me, scattereth."

questions.prompt: The Lord says through Jeremiah: "Hearken to my voice, and I will be your ____, and you shall be my people."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:23 reads: "Hearken to my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the coming of God's kingdom mean?
