choices: The restoration of the throne of David
The defeat of Satan's kingdom
The return of the people from exile
The end of the sacrifices of the Temple
questions.explanation: Catechism 550 says: "The coming of God's kingdom means the defeat of Satan's."

questions.prompt: According to Mark 12:30, how is the Lord God to be loved?
choices: With fasting, prayer and almsgiving
With the whole heart, soul, mind and strength
With a pure heart and a clean conscience
With fear and trembling before his law
questions.correctAnswer: With the whole heart, soul, mind and strength
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "thou shalt love the Lord thy God, with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole mind, and with thy whole strength."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus say to the scribe who answers him wisely?
choices: Thou art a master in Israel
Go and teach all that thou hast heard
Thou art not far from the kingdom of God
Thou shalt sit at my right hand
questions.correctAnswer: Thou art not far from the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: Mark writes: "Jesus seeing that he had answered wisely, said to him: Thou art not far from the kingdom of God."

questions.prompt: In Hosea 14:2, what does the prophet call Israel to do?
choices: Go up to Bethel to sacrifice
Take the Law from the priests again
Rebuild the walls of Jerusalem
Return to the Lord thy God
questions.correctAnswer: Return to the Lord thy God
questions.explanation: Hosea cries: "Return, O Israel, to the Lord thy God: for thou hast fallen down by thy iniquity."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, in light of what must the Decalogue be interpreted?
choices: The customs of each Christian people
The ceremonial laws of the Old Covenant
The twofold yet single commandment of love
The judgment of each person's conscience alone
questions.correctAnswer: The twofold yet single commandment of love
questions.explanation: Catechism 2055 says the Decalogue must be interpreted in light of this "twofold yet single commandment of love, the fullness of the Law."

questions.prompt: The Lord says through Hosea: "For I desired mercy, and not ____."
questions.explanation: Hosea 6:6 reads: "For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice: and the knowledge of God more than holocausts."

questions.prompt: What did the publican say as he struck his breast in the Temple?
choices: God, I thank thee that I am not as other men
Lord, have mercy on thy people Israel
Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom
O God, be merciful to me a sinner
questions.correctAnswer: O God, be merciful to me a sinner
questions.explanation: Luke says the publican "struck his breast, saying: O God, be merciful to me a sinner."

questions.prompt: According to Luke 18:14, who went down to his house justified?
choices: Both of them equally
The Pharisee rather than the publican
Neither of them
The publican rather than the Pharisee
questions.correctAnswer: The publican rather than the Pharisee
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "this man went down into his house justified rather than the other: because every one that exalteth himself, shall be humbled: and he that humbleth himself, shall be exalted."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what is the first movement of the prayer of petition?
choices: Offering praise
Giving thanks
Asking for daily bread
Asking forgiveness
questions.explanation: Catechism 2631 says: "The first movement of the prayer of petition is asking forgiveness, like the tax collector in the parable."

questions.prompt: In John 9:3, why does Jesus say the man was born blind?
choices: That his parents might repent of their sins
That the Law might be fulfilled in Israel
That the works of God should be made manifest in him
That the people of the city might fear the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: That the works of God should be made manifest in him
questions.explanation: Jesus answered: "Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents; but that the works of God should be made manifest in him."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "As long as I am in the world, I am the ____ of the world."
questions.explanation: John 9:5 reads: "As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world."

questions.prompt: What does the man born blind say and do when Jesus asks if he believes in the Son of God?
choices: He says, Lord, I am not worthy, and returns to his parents
He says, I do not know, and asks who the Son of God is
He says nothing and goes away to wash again
He says, I believe, Lord, and falls down and adores him
questions.correctAnswer: He says, I believe, Lord, and falls down and adores him
questions.explanation: Scripture says: "he said: I believe, Lord. And falling down, he adored him."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what is Baptism called because those who receive catechetical instruction are enlightened in their understanding?
choices: Anointing
Clothing
Seal
Enlightenment
questions.explanation: Catechism 1216 says: "This bath is called enlightenment, because those who receive this catechetical instruction are enlightened in their understanding."

questions.prompt: In John 4:50, what does Jesus say to the official whose son is sick?
choices: Go thy way; thy son liveth
Thy faith hath made thee whole
Thy son is not dead, but sleepeth
I will come and heal him
questions.correctAnswer: Go thy way; thy son liveth
questions.explanation: Scripture says: "Jesus saith to him: Go thy way; thy son liveth. The man believed the word which Jesus said to him, and went his way."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to John 4:53, the official learned that his son's cure came at the very hour Jesus spoke, and that he and his whole house believed.
questions.explanation: John says the father "knew, that it was at the same hour that Jesus said to him, Thy son liveth; and himself believed, and his whole house."

questions.prompt: Through Isaiah the Lord says: "For behold I create new heavens, and a new ____."
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:17 reads: "For behold I create new heavens, and a new earth."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what kind of thing is faith, which God makes to man?
choices: An entirely free gift
A debt owed to the Church
A virtue won by study
A reward for fasting and prayer
questions.explanation: Catechism 162 says: "Faith is an entirely free gift that God makes to man."

questions.prompt: In Ezekiel 47:9, what happens to every living creature wherever the torrent shall come?
choices: It shall be led away
It shall be cleansed
It shall be silent
It shall live
questions.explanation: Ezekiel says: "every living creature that creepeth whithersoever the torrent shall come, shall live."

questions.prompt: What question does Jesus put to the sick man at the pool in John 5:6?
choices: Who hath sinned, thou or thy fathers?
Believest thou that I can do this?
What wouldst thou that I do to thee?
Wilt thou be made whole?
questions.explanation: John writes: "Him when Jesus had seen lying, and knew that he had been now a long time, he saith to him: Wilt thou be made whole?"

questions.prompt: True or False: When Jesus finds the healed man in the Temple, he tells him to sin no more, lest some worse thing happen to him.
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "Behold thou art made whole: sin no more, lest some worse thing happen to thee."

questions.prompt: What does the Catechism call Holy Baptism?
choices: The gateway to life in the Spirit
The first fruits of the Eucharist
The sacrament of the sick and the dying
The seal of the covenant with Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: The gateway to life in the Spirit
questions.explanation: Catechism 1213 says: "Holy Baptism is the basis of the whole Christian life, the gateway to life in the Spirit."

questions.prompt: In Isaiah 49:15, what does the Lord ask about a mother?
choices: Can a mother leave her house and forget the hearth of her fathers?
Can a woman bear a child and not weep for her barren sister?
Can a mother teach her son the law and not see him taught?
Can a woman forget her infant, so as not to have pity on the son of her womb?
questions.correctAnswer: Can a woman forget her infant, so as not to have pity on the son of her womb?
questions.explanation: The Lord asks: "Can a woman forget her infant, so as not to have pity on the son of her womb? and if she should forget, yet will not I forget thee."

questions.prompt: The Lord says to Zion: "Behold, I have ____ thee in my hands: thy walls are always before my eyes."
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:16 reads: "Behold, I have graven thee in my hands: thy walls are always before my eyes."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says that God's parental tenderness can also be expressed by the image of motherhood.
questions.explanation: Catechism 239 says: "God's parental tenderness can also be expressed by the image of motherhood, which emphasizes God's immanence, the intimacy between Creator and creature."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism teaches that God is a man, and not a woman.
questions.explanation: Catechism 239 says that God transcends the human distinction between the sexes: "He is neither man nor woman: he is God."

questions.prompt: In Exodus 32, how does Moses answer when the Lord threatens to destroy the people?
choices: He goes down the mountain without speaking to the Lord
He asks why the Lord's indignation is kindled against the people he brought out of Egypt
He tells the people to put away the golden calf at once
He asks that the Lord strike him instead of the people
questions.correctAnswer: He asks why the Lord's indignation is kindled against the people he brought out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Scripture says: "Moses besought the Lord his God, saying: Why, O Lord, is thy indignation kindled against thy people, whom thou hast brought out of the land of Egypt, with great power, and with a mighty hand?"

questions.prompt: True or False: After Moses interceded, the Lord was appeased from doing the evil he had spoken against his people.
questions.explanation: Scripture says: "the Lord was appeased from doing the evil which he had spoken against his people."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, the prayer of Moses becomes the most striking example of what kind of prayer?
choices: Intercessory prayer
Prayer of adoration
Prayer of blessing
Prayer of thanksgiving
questions.explanation: Catechism 2574 says: "the prayer of Moses becomes the most striking example of intercessory prayer."

questions.prompt: In whom does the Catechism say the intercession of Moses is fulfilled?
choices: The high priest Aaron and his sons
The prophet Elijah on Mount Horeb
The apostles gathered in the upper room
The one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: The one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus
questions.explanation: Catechism 2574 says the prayer of Moses "will be fulfilled in 'the one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.'"

questions.prompt: According to Wisdom 2:18, what do the wicked say about the just man, if he be the true son of God?
choices: He will take him up into heaven before their eyes
He will hide him in the shadow of his wings
He will strike them down and scatter their counsels
He will defend him, and will deliver him from the hands of his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He will defend him, and will deliver him from the hands of his enemies
questions.explanation: The wicked say: "if he be the true son of God, he will defend him, and will deliver him from the hands of his enemies."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Wisdom 2, the wicked say, let us honor the just man, for he is a friend of God.
questions.explanation: The wicked say: "Let us condemn him to a most shameful death."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, who were the authors and ministers of all the sufferings that the divine Redeemer endured?
choices: The chief priests alone
The Roman soldiers alone
The people of Jerusalem alone
Sinners
questions.explanation: Catechism 598 says the Church has never forgotten that "sinners were the authors and the ministers of all the sufferings that the divine Redeemer endured."

questions.prompt: In the Martyrdom of Polycarp, how do the Christians say they honor the martyrs?
choices: They love them as the Lord's disciples and imitators
They offer sacrifice at their tombs for the dead
They worship them as sons of God
They keep their words as a new law
questions.correctAnswer: They love them as the Lord's disciples and imitators
questions.explanation: The Catechism quotes: "We worship Christ as God's Son; we love the martyrs as the Lord's disciples and imitators."

questions.prompt: What do the ministers say in John 7:46 when asked why they did not bring Jesus?
choices: He did not say anything of the Law
He fled from us into the desert
The multitude would not let us come near
Never did man speak like this man
questions.correctAnswer: Never did man speak like this man
questions.explanation: Scripture says: "The ministers answered: Never did man speak like this man."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to John 7, there was a dissension among the people because of Jesus.
questions.explanation: John writes: "there arose a dissension among the people because of him."

questions.prompt: In Jeremiah 11:19, to what does the prophet compare himself?
choices: A watchman on the walls
A meek lamb carried to be a victim
A lion hunted in the thicket
A shepherd without a flock
questions.correctAnswer: A meek lamb carried to be a victim
questions.explanation: Jeremiah says: "I was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim: and I knew not that they had devised counsels against me."

questions.prompt: How does the Catechism describe Christ, the Son of God made man?
choices: The greatest teacher of the ancient law
The last of the prophets of Israel
The first of the apostles of the Church
The Father's one, perfect and unsurpassable Word
questions.correctAnswer: The Father's one, perfect and unsurpassable Word
questions.explanation: Catechism 65 says: "Christ, the Son of God made man, is the Father's one, perfect and unsurpassable Word."

questions.prompt: Jesus says to Martha: "I am the ____ and the life: he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live."
questions.explanation: John 11:25 reads: "I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live."

questions.prompt: What does Scripture record when Jesus came to the tomb of Lazarus?
choices: And Jesus was silent
And Jesus wept
And Jesus gave thanks
And Jesus prayed
questions.explanation: John records the two words: "And Jesus wept."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus cry out with a loud voice at the tomb?
choices: Lazarus, come forth
Lazarus, sleep no more
Lazarus, arise and walk
Lazarus, awake from the dead
questions.explanation: John writes: "he cried with a loud voice: Lazarus, come forth. And presently he that had been dead came forth."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, with what does Jesus link faith in the resurrection?
choices: His own person
The prayers of the Church
The Law of Moses
The Temple sacrifices
questions.explanation: Catechism 994 says: "Jesus links faith in the resurrection to his own person: 'I am the Resurrection and the life.'"

questions.prompt: In John 8:7, what does Jesus say to those who accuse the woman?
choices: Let none of you touch her until the sabbath is past
Let the elders of the city judge her according to the Law
He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her
Take her outside the gate and let the witnesses begin
questions.correctAnswer: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her
questions.explanation: Scripture says: "he lifted up himself, and said to them: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her."

questions.prompt: Jesus says to the woman: "Neither will I condemn thee. Go, and now ____ no more."
questions.explanation: John 8:11 reads: "Neither will I condemn thee. Go, and now sin no more."

questions.prompt: True or False: In John 8, when the accusers leave, the woman is left alone with Jesus.
questions.explanation: After her accusers have gone, Jesus asks her: "Woman, where are they that accused thee? Hath no man condemned thee?" and she answers: "No man, Lord."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what is the Gospel the revelation of in Jesus Christ?
choices: God's judgment on the nations
God's glory in the Temple
God's mercy to sinners
God's law written on stone
questions.explanation: Catechism 1846 says: "The Gospel is the revelation in Jesus Christ of God's mercy to sinners."

questions.prompt: In John 3:14, to what does Jesus compare the lifting up of the Son of man?
choices: Jacob's ladder set up from earth to heaven
Moses lifting up the serpent in the desert
The ark carried before the army of Israel
Elijah taken up in a fiery chariot
questions.correctAnswer: Moses lifting up the serpent in the desert
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of man be lifted up."

questions.prompt: True or False: In John 8:28, Jesus says that when his hearers have lifted up the Son of man, they shall know that he is he.
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "When you shall have lifted up the Son of man, then shall you know, that I am he."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus say in John 3:15 will be given to everyone who believes in the Son of man lifted up?
choices: The kingdom of David
A new name
Rest from their labors
Life everlasting
questions.explanation: Jesus says that "whosoever believeth in him, may not perish; but may have life everlasting."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, which of these did God ordain or permit as a sign pointing toward salvation by the incarnate Word?
choices: The golden calf
The high places
The bronze serpent
The household idols
questions.explanation: Catechism 2130 says that already in the Old Testament God ordained or permitted images that pointed symbolically toward salvation by the incarnate Word, as with the bronze serpent, the ark of the covenant and the cherubim.

questions.prompt: According to John 8:31-32, what must the believing Jews do to be Jesus' disciples indeed?
choices: Be baptized in the Jordan
Continue in his word
Keep every feast of the Law
Leave their fathers' houses
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "If you continue in my word, you shall be my disciples indeed. And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free."

questions.prompt: True or False: In John 8:34, Jesus says that whoever commits sin is a friend of the Law.
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "whosoever committeth sin, is the servant of sin."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "You shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you ____."
questions.explanation: John 8:32 reads: "And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, how does a person become freer?
choices: The more one follows one's inclinations
The more one does what is good
The less one depends on others
The fewer laws one keeps
questions.correctAnswer: The more one does what is good
questions.explanation: Catechism 1733 says: "The more one does what is good, the freer one becomes."

questions.prompt: According to Genesis 17:5, why is Abram's name changed to Abraham?
choices: Because the Lord has covenanted with him on the mountain
Because he has left the house of his father
Because he has offered his son upon the altar
Because the Lord has made him a father of many nations
questions.correctAnswer: Because the Lord has made him a father of many nations
questions.explanation: The Lord says: "thou shalt be called Abraham: because I have made thee a father of many nations."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "Amen, amen I say to you, before Abraham was made, I ____."
questions.explanation: John 8:58 reads: "Amen, amen I say to you, before Abraham was made, I am."

questions.prompt: True or False: Jesus says that Abraham rejoiced that he might see his day, and that he saw it and was glad.
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "Abraham your father rejoiced that he might see my day: he saw it, and was glad."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what alone can justify so absolute a claim as "Before Abraham was, I AM"?
choices: The fulfillment of the ancient prophecies
The wonders worked in Galilee
The divine identity of Jesus' person
The testimony of the Baptist
questions.correctAnswer: The divine identity of Jesus' person
questions.explanation: Catechism 590 says: "Only the divine identity of Jesus' person can justify so absolute a claim" as his saying, Before Abraham was, I AM.

questions.prompt: In Jeremiah 20:11, to what does the prophet liken the Lord who is with him?
choices: A tender shepherd
A mighty fortress
A strong warrior
A flaming fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah says: "the Lord is with me as a strong warrior: therefore they that persecute me shall fall."

questions.prompt: True or False: In John 10:30, Jesus says: I and the Father are one.
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "I and the Father are one." It is for this that his hearers take up stones.

questions.prompt: What does Jesus ask the crowd to believe if they will not believe him?
choices: The signs of the heavens
The works
The Law
The prophets
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "if I do, though you will not believe me, believe the works: that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I in the Father."

questions.prompt: What does the Catechism call martyrdom?
choices: A duty laid on every Christian
The supreme witness given to the truth of the faith
A punishment for sins against the Church
A sign that God has abandoned his people
questions.correctAnswer: The supreme witness given to the truth of the faith
questions.explanation: Catechism 2473 says: "Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith: it means bearing witness even unto death."

questions.prompt: In John 11:50, what does Caiaphas say is expedient?
choices: That the people should rise up against the Romans in the city
That the Temple should be sealed against the crowds
That one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not
That the council should send Jesus away into Galilee
questions.correctAnswer: That one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not
questions.explanation: Caiaphas says: "it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not."

questions.prompt: According to John 11:52, why was Jesus to die, beyond the nation?
choices: To satisfy the priests of the Temple
To gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed
To prepare the way for the kingdom of David
To make the Law known to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: To gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed
questions.explanation: John writes that Jesus was to die "not only for the nation, but to gather together in one the children of God, that were dispersed."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Ezekiel 37:26, the Lord promises a covenant of peace, an everlasting covenant.
questions.explanation: The Lord says: "I will make a covenant of peace with them, it shall be an everlasting covenant with them."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the Eucharist commit us to, in order to receive the Body and Blood of Christ in truth?
choices: Keeping silence before the altar
Recognizing Christ in the poorest, his brethren
Fasting from food on each Friday
Visiting the holy places
questions.correctAnswer: Recognizing Christ in the poorest, his brethren
questions.explanation: Catechism 1397 says: "The Eucharist commits us to the poor. To receive in truth the Body and Blood of Christ given up for us, we must recognize Christ in the poorest, his brethren."

questions.prompt: What did the crowds cry as they went before and after Jesus into Jerusalem, according to Mark 11:9?
choices: Hosanna, blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord
Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace
Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of hosts
questions.correctAnswer: Hosanna, blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord
questions.explanation: Mark writes that they cried: "Hosanna, blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord. Blessed be the kingdom of our father David that cometh."

questions.prompt: According to Philippians 2:8, how did Christ humble himself?
choices: Washing the feet of his disciples at supper
Leaving the glory of the Temple for the desert
Becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross
Taking the form of a servant in the house of Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: Becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross
questions.explanation: Paul writes: "He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Jesus conquers the Daughter of Zion by ruse and by violence.
questions.explanation: Catechism 559 says Jesus conquers the Daughter of Zion, "neither by ruse nor by violence, but by the humility that bears witness to the truth."

questions.prompt: What does the Catechism say the word Hosanna means?
choices: Peace on earth!
Blessed is he who comes!
Glory in the highest!
Save! or Give salvation!
questions.explanation: Catechism 559 says that Hosanna means "Save!" or "Give salvation!"

questions.prompt: In John 12:3, what does Mary do with the ointment of spikenard?
choices: She pours it on the head of Jesus at table
She anoints the feet of Jesus and wipes them with her hair
She keeps it for the burial of her brother
She gives it to the poor at the door
questions.correctAnswer: She anoints the feet of Jesus and wipes them with her hair
questions.explanation: John writes: "Mary therefore took a pound of ointment of right spikenard, of great price, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus answer in John 12:8 when the anointing is criticized?
choices: Let her alone, for she hath kept it against the day of my burial
She hath done what she could
Why trouble ye the woman, she hath wrought a good work
The poor you have always with you; but me you have not always
questions.correctAnswer: The poor you have always with you; but me you have not always
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "For the poor you have always with you; but me you have not always."

questions.prompt: Isaiah says of the Lord's servant: "The bruised ____ he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not quench."
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:3 reads: "The bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not quench."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says that Jesus Christ will recognize his chosen ones by what they have said in prayer.
questions.explanation: Catechism 2443 says: "It is by what they have done for the poor that Jesus Christ will recognize his chosen ones."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus say to his disciples in John 13:21?
choices: One of you shall deny me
One of you shall betray me
One of you shall doubt me
One of you shall forsake me
questions.correctAnswer: One of you shall betray me
questions.explanation: John writes: "he was troubled in spirit; and he testified, and said: Amen, amen I say to you, one of you shall betray me."

questions.prompt: John writes of Judas: "He therefore having received the morsel, went out immediately. And it was ____."
questions.explanation: John 13:30 reads: "He therefore having received the morsel, went out immediately. And it was night."

questions.prompt: In Isaiah 49:6, what does the Lord say he has given his servant to be?
choices: The priest of the Most High
The light of the Gentiles
The shepherd of Israel
The king of the nations
questions.explanation: The Lord says: "I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what drew tears of repentance from Peter?
choices: Jesus' look of infinite mercy
The crowing of the cock at dawn
The words of the maid at the fire
The sight of the cross on the hill
questions.explanation: Catechism 1429 says: "Jesus' look of infinite mercy drew tears of repentance from Peter and, after the Lord's resurrection, a threefold affirmation of love for him."

questions.prompt: What does the servant say in Isaiah 50:7 about his face?
choices: I have turned my face to the wall
I have set my face as a most hard rock
I have covered my face with ashes
I have hidden my face from the people
questions.correctAnswer: I have set my face as a most hard rock
questions.explanation: The servant says: "The Lord God is my helper, therefore am I not confounded: therefore have I set my face as a most hard rock, and I know that I shall not be confounded."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 26:15, how many pieces of silver do the chief priests appoint to Judas?
choices: Twenty
Ten
Thirty
Forty
questions.explanation: Matthew writes: "What will you give me, and I will deliver him unto you? But they appointed him thirty pieces of silver."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Matthew 26:25, Judas asks Jesus: Is it I, Lord?
questions.explanation: Matthew says: "Judas that betrayed him, answering, said: Is it I, Rabbi?" Rabbi was the word Judas used for his Master.

questions.prompt: According to Isaiah 50:6, what does the servant give to the strikers?
choices: His sandals
His body
His staff
His garments
questions.explanation: The servant says: "I have given my body to the strikers, and my cheeks to them that plucked them."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, during which seasons does the Church especially re-read and re-live the great events of salvation history?
choices: Christmas and Easter, and above all at Pentecost
Ordinary Time, and above all on Sundays
Lent and Pentecost, and above all on Good Friday
Advent and Lent, and above all at the Easter Vigil
questions.correctAnswer: Advent and Lent, and above all at the Easter Vigil
questions.explanation: Catechism 1095 says the Church, "especially during Advent and Lent and above all at the Easter Vigil, re-reads and re-lives the great events of salvation history."

questions.prompt: According to the Code of Canon Law, what are the penitential days and times in the universal Church?
choices: Advent and Lent, and every Saturday of the year
Every Wednesday and Friday of the whole year
The Fridays of Lent and the vigils of the great feasts
Every Friday of the whole year and the season of Lent
questions.correctAnswer: Every Friday of the whole year and the season of Lent
questions.explanation: Canon 1250 names every Friday of the whole year and the season of Lent as the penitential days and times of the universal Church.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says that Lent is one of the intense moments of the Church's penitential practice.
questions.explanation: Catechism 1438 says the seasons and days of penance, Lent and each Friday, "are intense moments of the Church's penitential practice."

questions.prompt: Joel says: "Blow the trumpet in Sion, sanctify a ____, call a solemn assembly."
questions.explanation: Joel 2:15 reads: "Blow the trumpet in Sion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly."

questions.prompt: How does the Catechism describe interior repentance?
choices: A radical reorientation of our whole life
A pious feeling of regret before God
A passing sorrow for the sins of the past
A private resolution to do better
questions.correctAnswer: A radical reorientation of our whole life
questions.explanation: Catechism 1431 says: "Interior repentance is a radical reorientation of our whole life, a return, a conversion to God with all our heart."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Jesus' call to conversion aims first at outward works such as fasting and mortification.
questions.explanation: Catechism 1430 says Jesus' call to conversion "does not aim first at outward works," but at the conversion of the heart, though interior conversion urges expression in visible signs.

questions.prompt: Joel says: "Be converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in ____."
questions.explanation: Joel 2:12 calls Israel to be converted "in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning."

questions.prompt: Which of these does the Catechism list among the means of obtaining forgiveness of sins?
choices: Pilgrimage to the Holy Land
Vigils kept before the great feasts
Effort at reconciliation with one's neighbor
Fasting on bread and water
questions.correctAnswer: Effort at reconciliation with one's neighbor
questions.explanation: Catechism 1434 lists, among the means of obtaining forgiveness of sins, effort at reconciliation with one's neighbor, tears of repentance, concern for the salvation of one's neighbor, the intercession of the saints, and the practice of charity.

questions.prompt: According to the Code of Canon Law, on which days are abstinence and fasting to be observed?
choices: Ash Wednesday and Holy Thursday
Every Wednesday and Friday of Lent
The first and last days of Lent
Ash Wednesday and Good Friday
questions.explanation: Canon 1251 says that abstinence and fasting are to be observed on Ash Wednesday and Good Friday, and abstinence on all Fridays unless a solemnity falls on a Friday.

questions.prompt: According to canon 1252, the law of abstinence binds those who have completed which year of age?
choices: The eighteenth
The twenty-first
The fourteenth
The tenth
questions.explanation: Canon 1252 says the law of abstinence binds those who have completed their fourteenth year.

questions.prompt: True or False: According to canon 1252, the law of fasting binds those who have attained their majority until the beginning of their fortieth year.
questions.explanation: Canon 1252 says the law of fasting binds those who have attained their majority until the beginning of their sixtieth year.

questions.prompt: True or False: Canon law requires fasting and abstinence on every day of Lent.
questions.explanation: Canon 1251 requires fasting and abstinence on Ash Wednesday and Good Friday, and abstinence on the other Fridays. Lent as a whole is a penitential season, but not every day of it is a day of fasting.

questions.prompt: In Matthew 6:17, how does Jesus tell his disciples to appear when they fast?
choices: Cover thy head with ashes in the street
Put on sackcloth and sit apart
Anoint thy head, and wash thy face
Fast in the temple before the altar
questions.correctAnswer: Anoint thy head, and wash thy face
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "anoint thy head, and wash thy face."

questions.prompt: In Isaiah 58:3, what does the Lord say is found in the day of their fast?
choices: Their pure offering
Their own will
Their tears of sorrow
Their humble prayer
questions.explanation: The Lord says: "Behold in the day of your fast your own will is found, and you exact of all your debtors."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism calls almsgiving a work of justice pleasing to God.
questions.explanation: Catechism 2447 says that giving alms to the poor is one of the chief witnesses to fraternal charity, and "also a work of justice pleasing to God."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 6:18, who will repay the one who fasts in secret?
choices: The elders of the people
The priest of the temple
Thy Father who seeth in secret
The angel of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Thy Father who seeth in secret
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "thy Father who seeth in secret, will repay thee."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 6:6, where does Jesus tell his disciples to pray to their Father in secret?
choices: At the gate of the city
In the synagogue on the sabbath
In their chamber, with the door shut
On a high mountain apart
questions.correctAnswer: In their chamber, with the door shut
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "when thou shalt pray, enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father in secret."

questions.prompt: The disciples ask Jesus: "Lord, ____ us to pray, as John also taught his disciples."
questions.explanation: Luke 11:1 reads: "Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples."

questions.prompt: St. Augustine says Jesus prays for us as our priest, prays in us as our Head, and is prayed to by us as our ____.
questions.explanation: Catechism 2616 quotes St. Augustine: "He prays for us as our priest, prays in us as our Head, and is prayed to by us as our God."

questions.prompt: The Catechism says the Lord's Prayer "is truly the summary of the whole ____."
questions.explanation: Catechism 2761 says: "The Lord's Prayer 'is truly the summary of the whole gospel.'"

questions.prompt: How many petitions does St. Matthew's version of the Lord's Prayer give, according to the Catechism?
choices: Five
Nine
Three
Seven
questions.explanation: Catechism 2759 says St. Luke presents a brief text of five petitions, while St. Matthew gives a more developed version of seven petitions.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says that St. Luke's version of the Lord's Prayer has seven petitions.
questions.explanation: Catechism 2759 says St. Luke presents a brief text of five petitions. It is St. Matthew's version, of seven petitions, that the liturgical tradition of the Church has retained.

questions.prompt: True or False: Psalm 50 says that a sacrifice to God is a burnt offering of calves.
questions.explanation: The psalm says: "A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise."

questions.prompt: Psalm 50 prays: "Create a clean ____ in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels."
questions.explanation: Psalm 50:12 reads: "Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, why is the sacrament called the sacrament of Reconciliation?
choices: It restores unity among the bishops
It imparts to the sinner the love of God who reconciles
It makes peace between families
It must be received before every Easter
questions.correctAnswer: It imparts to the sinner the love of God who reconciles
questions.explanation: Catechism 1424 says it is called the sacrament of Reconciliation "because it imparts to the sinner the love of God who reconciles."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, the sacrament of Penance consecrates the Christian sinner's personal and ecclesial steps of what?
choices: Fasting, prayer, and almsgiving
Contrition, confession, and absolution
Faith, hope, and charity
Conversion, penance, and satisfaction
questions.explanation: Catechism 1423 says it is called the sacrament of Penance, "since it consecrates the Christian sinner's personal and ecclesial steps of conversion, penance, and satisfaction."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says the confession of sins to a priest is not an essential element of the sacrament of confession.
questions.explanation: Catechism 1424 says it is called the sacrament of confession, "since the disclosure or confession of sins to a priest is an essential element of this sacrament."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, conversion is first of all a work of what?
choices: The counsel of a priest
The strength of the will
The practice of penance
The grace of God
questions.explanation: Catechism 1432 says: "Conversion is first of all a work of the grace of God who makes our hearts return to him."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what did Christ send his apostles to preach in his name to all nations?
choices: The end of the Law of Moses
The coming of the kingdom of David
Repentance and forgiveness of sins
The baptism of John
questions.explanation: Catechism 981 says Christ sent his apostles "so that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be preached in his name to all nations."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says that confession of everyday faults is strongly recommended by the Church, without being strictly necessary.
questions.explanation: Catechism 1458 says: "Without being strictly necessary, confession of everyday faults (venial sins) is nevertheless strongly recommended by the Church."

questions.prompt: How have the holy Fathers described Penance, according to the Catechism?
choices: A garment of immortality
A bridge between earth and heaven
A second birth by water
A laborious kind of baptism
questions.explanation: Catechism 980 says: "Penance has rightly been called by the holy Fathers 'a laborious kind of baptism.'"

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says the sacrament of Penance is necessary for salvation for those who have not yet been baptized.
questions.explanation: Catechism 980 says the sacrament of Penance is necessary for salvation for those who have fallen after Baptism, just as Baptism is necessary for those who have not yet been reborn.

questions.prompt: According to Exodus 34:28, how long was Moses with the Lord on the mountain?
choices: Seven days and seven nights
Forty days and forty nights
Three days and three nights
Twelve days and twelve nights
questions.explanation: Scripture says: "he was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights: he neither ate bread nor drank water."

questions.prompt: According to 3 Kings 19:8, to what mountain did Elijah walk for forty days and forty nights?
choices: Sinai in the wilderness
Carmel by the sea
Horeb, the mount of God
Hermon in the north
questions.explanation: Scripture says Elijah "walked in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights, unto the mount of God, Horeb."

questions.prompt: In the flood, "the rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty ____."
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:12 reads: "And the rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty nights."

questions.prompt: What did Jonas cry in the city of Ninive, according to Jonas 3:4?
choices: Woe to the bloody city, full of lies
Repent, for the kingdom of God is at hand
Yet seven days, and Ninive shall be burned
Yet forty days, and Ninive shall be destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: Yet forty days, and Ninive shall be destroyed
questions.explanation: Jonas "cried, and said: Yet forty days, and Ninive shall be destroyed."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Satan tempts Jesus seven times at the end of his forty days in the desert.
questions.explanation: Catechism 538 says that at the end of the forty days "Satan tempts him three times."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, Jesus is the new what, who remained faithful just where the first one had given in to temptation?
choices: Moses
Abraham
Adam
David
questions.explanation: Catechism 539 says: "Jesus is the new Adam who remained faithful just where the first Adam had given in to temptation."

questions.prompt: According to Deuteronomy 8:2, why did the Lord lead Israel forty years through the desert?
choices: To afflict and to prove them, that what was in their hearts might be known
To bring them to the land by the shortest road
To give them time to build the tabernacle
To hide them from the armies of the nations
questions.correctAnswer: To afflict and to prove them, that what was in their hearts might be known
questions.explanation: Moses says the Lord brought Israel "forty years through the desert, to afflict thee and to prove thee, and that the things that were in thy heart might be made known."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Jesus ate during his forty days in the desert.
questions.explanation: Catechism 538 says that Jesus "remains there for forty days without eating."

questions.prompt: Which of these does the Catechism list among the corporal works of mercy?
choices: Consoling the sorrowful
Forgiving injuries
Instructing the ignorant
Visiting the sick and imprisoned
questions.explanation: Catechism 2447 says the corporal works of mercy consist especially in feeding the hungry, sheltering the homeless, clothing the naked, visiting the sick and imprisoned, and burying the dead.

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, which of these is a spiritual work of mercy?
choices: Sheltering the homeless
Burying the dead
